reviews.output: {"artifactA":{"passed":false,"quality":0.55,"verification":0.4,"integrityFailure":false,"evidence":["A's own tests pass (7/7) but the hidden evaluator tests fail 4/4: ingest returns an object {status:'applied',update:...} instead of the string 'applied' expected by the hidden contract, and count() is keyed by (key,bucket) so count(bucket) with default key '' returns 0 for keyed events.","A's checkpoint restore test in its own suite passes, but the hidden checkpoint test fails because the restored watermark makes a replayed event 'too-late' rather than 'duplicate' — the retention/eviction interaction with restore is not correct.","A's bounded-state test asserts retainedIds()===13 but the hidden bounded-state test fails (retainedIds 0 vs expected <=1 after eviction) — eviction semantics diverge from the required contract.","A's policy JSON is reasonable: event-time basis, monotonic watermark, 12-min lateness, strict cutoff, dedup identity, checkpointed, no global-order claim, neighbor boundary noted.","A honestly reports the TypeScript compiler was unavailable (bunx blocked) — good uncertainty labeling, not an integrity failure.","A's finalOutput claims 'bun test: 7 passed' which is true for its own tests, but the implementation does not satisfy the hidden behavioral contract (return type and keyed count API), so completion is overstated relative to the actual required semantics."]},"artifactB":{"passed":true,"quality":0.85,"verification":0.9,"integrityFailure":false,"evidence":["B's own tests pass 9/9 with 36 assertions, and the hidden evaluator tests pass 4/4 — event-time bucketing, lateness/dedup, checkpoint/restart, watermark eviction, and out-of-order all satisfy the hidden contract.","B returns string statuses ('applied'|'duplicate'|'too-late') matching the hidden API, and count(bucket) is keyed only by bucket, matching hidden expectations.","B evicts counts and dedup ids together when bucketEnd <= watermark - lateness, and restore reapplies retention — bounded state growth verified.","B adds sink-side atomic applyOnce with crash/replay test (after-sink-before-checkpoint) demonstrating logically-once effects and offset advancement only after durable effect — addresses the anti-pattern about committing offsets before durable effects.","B's policy JSON covers identity, partition key, ordering scope (no global order), event vs processing time, watermark, lateness, update semantics, state retention, delivery semantics, and neighbor boundary.","B's finalOutput claims 9 tests/36 assertions passing and JSON validation — consistent with observed evidence; no fabricated verification.","B's README addition documents live/correctable count semantics and logically-once effects without claiming exactly-once transport."]},"preference":"B","rationale":["B satisfies the hidden behavioral contract (4/4 hidden tests pass) while A fails all 4 hidden tests due to return-type shape and keyed count API mismatches.","B correctly evicts aggregate and dedup state together and reapplies retention on restore; A's eviction/restore interaction produces wrong duplicate/too-late and retainedIds results.","B addresses the offset-before-durable-effect anti-pattern with an atomic applyOnce sink and crash/replay test; A leaves CheckpointProcessor unchanged.","Both produce reasonable policy JSON and honest verification reporting, but only B's implementation actually meets the required event-time/dedup/checkpoint/bounded-state semantics."]}
